steps.title: Introspect SQLite and Postgres schemas and declare Redis key patterns for entity metadata
steps.summary: A host-run read-only command that writes schema-only entity metadata from SQLite and Postgres catalogs and from reviewed Redis key-pattern declarations, with provenance that says it came from a live store at a time.

risk.notes: Credentials, production reach and false completeness. A bug could leak a connection string or row data, or present an introspected snapshot as current. Must fail closed and stay schema-only.

value.why: Entities for stores with no literal DDL in source, bounded by an approved credential and environment policy.

questions.ask: Which client libraries may PMO depend on?
questions.why: SQLite can use node:sqlite; Postgres and Redis need a driver, which adds a dependency to a tool that currently has none for stores.
questions.default: SQLite via node:sqlite; Postgres and Redis through optional peer dependencies the host installs, so PMO itself gains no store dependency.

steps.title: Count a PR merged into a stacked base as delivered once its content reached main
steps.summary: The PMO marks a merged PR as verified only when it targeted main and its merge commit is an ancestor of main. A PR merged into a stacked base is never verified, so it stays in the waiting queue as Merged; main verification pending although its content may already be on main. Verify such a PR when its head commit is an ancestor of main, or when a step in the approved plan on main dismisses it with a reviewed reason.

risk.notes: Changes only how a merged PR is classified in the local PR snapshot; it cannot clear an open PR or a prerequisite that is not merged. A supersession needs a reviewed reason in the plan on main. Generic source change: contributed upstream first, then recorded as a receipt (G-033).

value.why: Delivered work stays in the waiting queue, which hides PRs that really need review or merge.
